claims.text: The oxidation resistance and high-temperature integrity of multiprincipal-element alloys are governed by the relative oxidation and diffusion kinetics of their constituent elements.
Fast-diffusing, reactive elements such as Mn can dominate the surface oxidation reaction.
Mn-dominated oxidation produces non-protective oxide scales.
Mn-dominated oxide scales grow rapidly and compromise material integrity.
Increasing the surface concentration of slower-diffusing Cr or Hf promotes a continuous, adherent protective oxide such as Cr2O3.
The initial equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi alloy is homogeneously mixed and has a uniform microstructure and elemental distribution.
Reducing Mn and/or increasing Cr or Hf is expected to alter the alloy's oxidation behavior.
A pre-oxidation treatment can promote surface segregation of protective Cr or Hf.
Oxidation behavior should be compared in air at 1 atm over 500-1100 °C and in vacuum or inert atmosphere.
Oxide-scale phase, thickness, continuity, and adhesion mediate oxidation resistance and material integrity.
Differential elemental diffusion causes Mn to oxidize preferentially.
Preferential Mn oxidation causes bulk Mn depletion.
A thin Cr2O3-rich protective layer acts as a diffusion barrier that preserves alloy microstructure and mechanical integrity.
The modified alloy should form a thinner, more continuous, and more adherent protective oxide than equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
The modified alloy should show less near-surface depletion of key elements than the baseline.
The modified alloy should retain hardness, tensile properties, and integrity under thermal cycling better than the baseline.
Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi forms predominantly Mn-rich, non-protective oxides under high-temperature oxidation.
The baseline's Mn-rich oxide scales become thicker and cause mechanical-property degradation.
The proposed mechanism should apply from 500 °C to 1100 °C when oxidation and diffusion dominate surface behavior.
Failure of the modified alloy to produce a significantly thinner, more continuous, adherent protective oxide together with improved mechanical integrity would falsify the hypothesis.
